method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **The commonest cause is a (usually viral) URTI.** Investigations and treatment are rarely needed for well children with a short history.
claims.source_text: The most common cause of cough is an upper respiratory tract infection (usually viral in nature) … Investigations and treatment are rarely required for well children with a short history of cough
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Young children have 6–12 respiratory infections a year**; most coughs resolve without treatment in 1–3 weeks.
claims.source_text: Young children develop 6-12 respiratory tract infections per year, usually accompanied by cough. In most children, the cough is self-limiting, most resolve without treatment in 1-3 weeks
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Definitions:** acute = up to 2 weeks; protracted acute = daily for 2–4 weeks; **chronic = daily for more than 4 weeks**. Chronic cough warrants further assessment.
claims.source_text: Acute cough: lasting up to 2 weeks Protracted acute cough: daily cough lasting 2-4 weeks Chronic cough: daily cough lasting >4 weeks … Chronic cough warrants further assessment
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Persistent daily cough over 4 weeks: assess and investigate with CXR and spirometry (if able).**
claims.source_text: Children who have a persistent daily cough lasting >4 weeks should be assessed and investigated with a CXR and spirometry (if able), with consideration given to further investigations and management
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **First establish duration and whether the cough is wet or dry**, look for red flags, and identify specific causes or recent infection.
claims.source_text: determine duration of cough and whether wet or dry elicit red flag symptoms or findings that may indicate serious underlying disease identify causes of specific cough or recent respiratory infections
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Sudden onset without a viral prodrome, or after choking, may mean foreign body inhalation.** Onset in early infancy suggests aspiration, congenital airway abnormality or cystic fibrosis; choking with feeds suggests aspiration.
claims.source_text: Sudden onset without viral prodrome (or after choking episode) may suggest foreign body inhalation … Onset in early infancy may suggest aspiration, congenital airway abnormality or cystic fibrosis … Choking or coughing with feeding may suggest aspiration
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cough type:** daily wet morning cough → PBB, suppurative lung disease or bronchiectasis; paroxysmal → pertussis or foreign body; staccato in infants → chlamydia; barking → croup; honking, distractible → tic or somatic cough disorder.
claims.source_text: Daily, persistent, wet, often in morning: protracted bacterial bronchitis (PBB), chronic suppurative lung disease, bronchiectasis Paroxysmal: pertussis or foreign body Staccato: suggestive of chlamydia (in infants) Barking or seal-like (+/- stridor): croup … Dry, honking, barking, distractible, suggestible: tic or somatic cough disorder
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **More than 3 episodes of PBB in 12 months warrants referral** or investigation for chronic suppurative lung disease.
claims.source_text: (>3 episodes of PBB in 12-month period warrants referral/further investigation)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine for** infection, work of breathing, hypoxia, stridor, chest signs, faltering growth, cardiac failure, and clubbing or chest wall deformity (suppurative lung disease).
claims.source_text: Fever, coryza or other signs of acute infection Increased work of breathing, hypoxia, stridor, chest signs (wheeze, crackles, crepitations) Faltering growth (or growth failure) Signs of cardiac failure (oedema, hepatomegaly, heart murmur) Signs of chronic suppurative lung disease/bronchiectasis (clubbing, poor growth, chest wall deformity)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Red flags in chronic cough:** shortness of breath · recurrent chronic/wet cough · recurrent pneumonia · chest pain · **haemoptysis** · systemic symptoms (fever, weight loss, growth failure) · neurodevelopmental abnormality · feeding difficulties · stridor · abnormal examination, CXR or lung function · co-existing chronic disease.
claims.source_text: Red flags in chronic cough Shortness of breath (at rest or exertional) Recurrent episodes of chronic or wet or productive cough Recurrent pneumonia Chest pain Haemoptysis Systemic symptoms (fever, weight loss, growth failure) Neurodevelopmental abnormality Feeding difficulties (including choking/vomiting) Stridor and other respiratory noises Abnormal clinical respiratory examination (eg crackles, digital clubbing) Abnormal systemic examination (eg growth failure) Abnormal chest x-ray Abnormal lung function Co-existing chronic disease (eg immunodeficiency, syndromes)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Over-the-counter cough medicines and decongestants are not recommended** — no proven efficacy and potential safety risks.
claims.source_text: Over the counter cough medicines and decongestants are not recommended due to lack of proven efficacy and potential safety risks
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **No empiric antibiotics, steroids, proton pump inhibitors or antihistamines.**
claims.source_text: Empiric use of antibiotics, steroids, proton pump inhibitors and antihistamines are not recommended
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Honey has no strong evidence for cough** and carries risks — **infant botulism under 12 months**, dental caries and aspiration.
claims.source_text: Honey is often proposed as a treatment for cough, but there is no strong evidence supporting its effectiveness, and it carries risks such as infant botulism (in infants <12 months), dental caries and aspiration
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For every child:** advise avoiding airway irritants (smoking, vaping, wood-fire heaters), explain when to return (transition to chronic cough), and acknowledge parental concerns.
claims.source_text: All children presenting with cough should have education around avoidance of airway irritants eg cigarette smoking, vaping, e-cigarettes and wood-fire heaters understanding of when to seek repeat assessment (transition to chronic cough) acknowledgement of parental concerns and reassurance
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **PBB is the commonest cause of chronic wet cough**: the child is otherwise well, with no alternative cause, and investigations (including CXR apart from perihilar thickening) are normal.
claims.source_text: Most common cause of chronic wet cough in children. Children are otherwise well, with no alternative cause evident on history or examination and investigations (including chest x-ray, apart from perihilar thickening) are normal
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Start a 2-week course of amoxicillin/clavulanic acid 22.5 mg/kg (amoxicillin component, max 875 mg) bd.**
claims.source_text: Extended course of antibiotics. Start with 2-week course of Amoxicillin/clavulanic acid 22.5 mg/kg of amoxicillin component (max dose 875 mg) bd
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Penicillin hypersensitivity:** trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 4 mg/kg (trimethoprim component, max 160 mg) bd.
claims.source_text: Penicillin hypersensitivity: trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 4 mg/kg of trimethoprim component (max dose 160 mg) bd
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Still wet after 2 weeks: continue the same antibiotic for a further 2 weeks.** Still wet after 4 weeks, or more than 3 PBB episodes a year: investigate as for suppurative lung disease and refer.
claims.source_text: If wet cough persists after 2 weeks, continue same antibiotic for a further 2 weeks … If wet cough persists after 4 weeks or child has had >3 PBB episodes/year, consider further investigations (as per suppurative lung disease) and referral to paediatrician and/or paediatric respiratory physician
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Chronic suppurative lung disease / bronchiectasis** (wet cough unresponsive to PBB treatment or recurring off antibiotics): FBE, serum immunoglobulins, CXR, spirometry, sweat test, sputum culture; refer to a paediatric respiratory physician.
claims.source_text: Chronic wet cough, which is unresponsive to PBB treatment, or frequently recurs when antibiotics ceased … FBE, serum immunoglobulins (IgM, A, G), chest x-ray, spirometry (if able), sweat test, sputum culture Refer to paediatric respiratory physician for further assessment
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Interstitial lung disease:** chronic dry cough with diffuse inspiratory crepitations, tachypnoea, growth failure or hypoxia — refer to a paediatric respiratory physician.
claims.source_text: Interstitial lung disease Chronic (typically) dry cough. Diffuse inspiratory crepitations, tachypnoea, growth failure, hypoxia … Referral to paediatric respiratory physician for further assessment
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Somatic cough or tic disorder:** honking, disappears asleep or distracted — education and reassurance; consider distraction therapies, psychological support or hypnosis.
claims.source_text: Somatic cough or tic disorder Often honking, disappears when asleep or distracted. Repetitive throat clearing Education and reassurance Consider referral for distraction therapies, psychological support, hypnosis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Refer to a paediatric respiratory physician for:** chronic wet cough failing 4 weeks of antibiotics · more than 3 PBB episodes a year · chronic dry cough over 6 months failing treatment (e.g. an asthma trial) · specific cough or red flags.
claims.source_text: Consider referral to paediatric respiratory physician when Chronic wet cough and failure to respond to 4 weeks of appropriate antibiotics Recurrent episodes of chronic wet cough (>3 episodes of PBB/year) Chronic dry cough persisting >6 months and failure to respond to appropriate treatment (eg empiric trial of asthma treatment) Assessment is suggestive of specific cough, or red flags are present
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider discharge when** the child is stable and any investigations and follow-up are arranged.
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when Child is stable Investigations and follow up arranged if needed
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23
